question: Is the new hold route (POST /displays/{screen_id}/show) bound to the admitted owner — the door's authority, his own conversation and a record that conversation was issued — before any tool runs, any record is read or any screen changes, given that put_held calls dispatch without passing the request?
answer: Yes. The chain, at this commit. The door: app/main.py guard_and_freshness refuses a request proxy_state calls forged, a proxied one with no login and a login not on the allow-list, then for every path that is not public asks principal_verdict (app/routes/actions.py: his login on the list and, with CROOKS_TAILSCALE_VERIFY on — production's unset value resolves to on, config/settings.py — Tailscale confirming the device is his; a request made on the server itself only when CROOKS_WRITES_LOCAL_OWNER or CROOKS_LOCAL_OWNER says so, and both are off in production) and answers 403 before any route runs. Only then does it make the owner's authority (tool_authority.for_owner) and set it on the request's context (TOOL_AUTHORITY), revoking it once the answer has been sent. The screens router asks the same rule again as its own dependency (displays.router: Depends(require_principal)). The route: show_held -> put.put_held -> put._put, which refuses, in this order and before anything is dispatched or read: a kind a screen does not show (422; HeldBody takes session_id, kind and ref and nothing else); a conversation CLIVE has let go of (409 no_session) or one bound to another login (403 wrong_session, session_matches); a screen that is gone (404 not_found) or waiting for its code (409 not_approved); and a record THAT conversation was not issued — classify(SHOW_TOOL, args, session.issued_ids) is DENY, because screen_show's issued-id arguments (order_id, objective_id) are optional in its schema, so an absent one is skipped and a supplied one must be in the session's issued ids (gate._check_issued_ids) — 403 not_issued. Only then is dispatch called, with the session _conversation resolved and never with the request: authority does not travel in the request object, it is the context variable the door set. dispatch refuses when no active authority is held (tool_authority.current()), asks classify again against session.issued_ids and refuses a DENY before any handler; screen_show itself refuses any authority that is not OWNER (display_tools._owners_own) and a screen not approved, both before an order is read. So nothing the body carries can stand in for the owner or for the conversation: the authority is the door's, the conversation is the one this login holds, and the record must have been issued to it by one of its own reads. New at round 13, tests/test_r13_evidence_screens.py watches dispatch and DisplayStore.show while the admitted owner posts order 1938, issued to his conversation A, with his conversation B: 403 not_issued, dispatch never called, show never called, Shopify not read, the record of screens the same bytes; the same drop with A dispatches screen_show once and puts the slip up, so the watch is real. The route does not exist at 6a29e310 (no app/displays/put.py there).

question: With production's switches as configured (CROOKS_TAILSCALE_VERIFY and CROOKS_LOCAL_OWNER unset), how do the screen routes authenticate a caller, and how does a screen tool call pass through the gate — can a refused caller reach any screen route or tool, or a slip go up for an id the conversation was not issued?
answer: No. The routes: every screen route is behind the door (app/main.py guard_and_freshness asks principal_verdict for every path that is not public) and behind the screens router's own dependency, require_principal (app/routes/displays.py). Unset, config/settings.py resolves tailscale_verify=True and local_owner=False, and production's .env has CROOKS_WRITES_LOCAL_OWNER=false, so a forged forwarding header, a proxied request with no login, a stranger's login, his login on a device Tailscale does not confirm and the server's own request are each 403 before any route. The tools: a screen tool the model calls goes MaxAgentSDKProvider._dispatch (refused without the turn's active authority) -> dispatch (refused without tool_authority.current(); classify against the session's issued ids; a DENY before any handler) -> screen_show (display_tools._owners_own: OWNER authority only; an unapproved screen refused before an order is read). A slip needs a real lookup: screen_show's order_id is one of gate._ISSUED_ID_ARGS, so an id the conversation was not issued by its own read is 'NOT YET' and nothing is read or shown. The round-12 drop route runs the same gate for the conversation the drop names (app/displays/put.py; see the S3/S3-03 entry). The tests run, they are not only read: the named tests pass at this commit, and acceptance run 36567654914 (push, 361b0138) ran the whole offline suite with them in it: 5946 passed, 26 skipped, exit 0. test_on_productions_own_switches... deletes both variables from the environment and lets the app's own lifespan resolve them.

question: On the live provider, do Claude's tool calls keep the prepare-only boundary — does a write the model calls pass through the gate and stage a proposal, with no mutation executed before the owner's gesture?
answer: Yes. MaxAgentSDKProvider._options gives the Agent SDK no built-in tools (tools=[]), only CLIVE's in-process MCP server built from the registry, with the tools it withholds disallowed as well, permission_mode 'dontAsk', no settings inherited, and a PreToolUse hook (make_pretooluse_hook, app/tools/dispatch.py) that fires on every call and denies what the gate denies. The MCP server's handler for every tool is the provider's _dispatch: refused without the turn's active owner authority, refused once the owner has moved on, then dispatch() under that authority. dispatch classifies the call (app/tools/gate.py); a write classifies STAGE_FOR_OWNER and goes to _stage, which runs the tool's own prepare from a fresh read and hands the result to ActionEngine.stage — a PENDING proposal on the session, nothing sent. The only code that executes a write is ActionEngine.commit, and its only callers are POST /actions/{id}/commit (after the owner's gesture: for a red card, the arm, the hold and its token) and the batch route's; no path from the provider reaches it. The test runs the provider's own code, not a stand-in for it: tests/test_r11_turn.py `sdk` replaces only the `claude` subprocess (Cli), which runs the provider's own hook and its own in-process tool handler on a task carrying none of the request's context, as the SDK does; a refund, a cancellation and a store credit asked for out loud are each a red PENDING card, a commit without the hold is 409 not_armed, a spoken 'yes' applies nothing, the same change on a record the conversation never read is denied by the hook, and sdk.store.mutations == [] throughout.

question: Does the made-once write boundary stop a second order or credit being made from one card, for concurrent, unarmed and retried commits — is its reservation atomic, and is it correctly released afterwards?
answer: The reservation is atomic; its release is not bound to the commit that made it, and that is a real defect. Atomic: in POST /actions/{id}/commit, workspaces.commit_refused, workspaces.before_commit and the engine's claim run with no await between them (app/routes/actions.py: commit_refused, before_commit, then await runtime.actions.commit, whose code before `proposal.status = EXECUTING` awaits nothing, app/actions/engine.py). So of two hold cards from one card committed at once, the first to reach commit_refused marks the card `sending` and claims its proposal, and the second finds the mark: 409 already_made, its card withdrawn, nothing sent (test_s2a_03_two_hold_cards...: one completion, whichever request ran first). A retry of the same card while it is sending is the engine's: the proposal is EXECUTING, so it waits for the first commit's outcome and returns it (already_executed), one completion. A Prepare tapped meanwhile is refused (the card is `finished`). A commit without its hold is 409 not_armed and after_commit takes the mark off again, so the real hold still makes the one order. The defect: before_commit notes `sending, by=commit` against the workspace with no proposal id, and after_commit removes that note for ANY proposal of the workspace whose outcome is not VERIFIED, EXECUTED, UNVERIFIED or FAILED (app/families/_workspace.py, the last branch of after_commit). A commit of a hold card the same card withdrew earlier (REVOKED) or that expired passes commit_refused (it refuses PENDING cards only), gets `revoked` from the engine, and its after_commit removes the live hold's reservation while that hold is still at its precondition read (engine.commit awaits write.observe before the family's own ws.sending marks the card again). Until then the card is not finished: Prepare is taken, a new hold card is staged, and its commit passes commit_refused. Reproduced, and left failing as found (xfail strict): tests/test_r13_evidence_made_once.py::test_s2a_03_a_withdrawn_hold_card_committed_meanwhile_leaves_the_sending_card_finished — a £20 credit at its balance read, a withdrawn hold card of the same card committed, Prepare taken and the new card held, the first released: two store_credit_credit mutations, balance £55 from £15. What it takes: a commit POST for a withdrawn card of the same card (a page that has not caught up, or a second device) while another hold is at its precondition read, then a Prepare and a full hold inside that same read, and a read that answers with the balance from before the second credit. Orders are further held by their draft (a second completion of the same draft is Shopify's to refuse) and by the card's own digest (as_prepared); codes by the code being unique; a credit by nothing else. Production (6a29e310) has no made-once at all — no commit_refused, before_commit or after_commit — so this is a hole in new protection, not a regression. Round 12's follow-up ruled this finding a defect but the record does not print its reasoning, and followup-collected.json is only on the server (/root/clive-activation/round-12/); it is not recovered here. The one-proposal-per-request rule in ActionEngine.stage normally keeps two hold cards of one card from waiting at once; the concurrency test sets that aside so that the route's own check is what is tested.

question: After a store-credit send whose answer never came back, or with a second hold card prepared from the same card, is the card locked so that the account cannot be credited twice?
answer: Locked in two of the three cases a lost answer can come to; not in the third, and that is a real defect. store_credit._execute sends through ws.sending, which notes the card `sending` before the mutation leaves and `failed` only when the send certainly did not happen (never_left: Shopify refused it, or it was never sent). The engine then decides the lost answer with one re-read (ActionEngine._settle_by_observation). Balance read back as £35 after a £20 credit: VERIFIED, the card DONE. Balance unreadable: UNVERIFIED, and after_commit makes the card UNCONFIRMED. Either way `finished`: a second hold card from the same card is 409 already_made and Shopify is sent one credit (the three parametrised cases). The third: a read timeout is a request that left — ShopifyClient._post turns httpx.ReadTimeout into a plain ShopifyError, neither unsent nor refused — and Shopify can still apply it after the Mac has stopped waiting. When the re-read made at once still shows £15, _settle_by_observation finishes the proposal FAILED 'service_unavailable' (write.settle is None for a credit) and after_commit turns that into the card's FAILED, which is not finished: the card is redrawn 'Store credit · not given — The credit was not given: … Nothing was credited; prepare it again.' with Prepare live, while the spoken line says 'I couldn't confirm the credit'. A second hold card, already waiting or prepared from the handed-back card, then sends a second £20. Reproduced, and left failing as found (xfail strict): tests/test_r13_evidence_made_once.py::test_s2b_02_a_timed_out_credit_the_reread_finds_unmade_is_not_given_again (the second card's commit is 200, not 409; two mutations) and ::test_s2b_02_a_timed_out_credit_is_drawn_as_sent_not_confirmed_and_prepares_nothing (the card as he sees it; two credits). store_credit._execute's own comment says only a refusal or a send that never left marks the card failed; the engine's re-read is a third way in. The balance precondition on the second card stops it only if the first credit has landed between that card's Prepare and its commit. The engine rule is the same code at 6a29e310 (commit, _settle_by_observation and _prove are identical there, docstrings aside), and production has no made-once at all, so production is exposed at least as much. The same rule gives an order card back after a completion that left (see T3/T3-02).

question: After Prepare, does editing that same order by voice and by tap make its old hold card unable to complete a draft?
answer: Yes, three times over. (1) Every new sentence withdraws the half's waiting cards before the model is asked (app/routes/turn.py: revoke_pending, then advance_epoch). (2) Every change to the card — shopify_order_build by voice, order.field, order.choose, order.additem, order.removeitem by tap — reads what the card would make before and after (ws.card_state) and withdraws the hold cards prepared from it when that differs (order_create._touch -> ws.touched -> ws.withdraw -> engine.revoke_ids); a REVOKED card is terminal and the engine never sends it. (3) Beneath those, the floor: commit_refused compares the card's digest when it was prepared (facts._prepared) with what it would make now and refuses 409 'The card changed since this was prepared'; and the order's own precondition carries `as_prepared` (_observe -> ws.still_as_prepared), so even a commit that reached the engine would be stale. Round 13's route test prepares, arms the old hold card (its token in hand), says 'add five pounds postage' and types a note, then commits the old card with its token: not verified (revoked), zero draft_order_complete; prepared again, the hold makes one order, with the £5 postage the card now says. The second test changes the card without passing through any withdrawal and commits the old card with its token: 409, zero completions.

question: Can a store-credit or discount-code hold card whose card changed without passing through the withdrawal still be applied — the stale-card check shown for orders, for credits and codes?
answer: No. The floor is the workspace's, not the order family's: commit_refused (app/families/_workspace.py) refuses any PENDING hold card whose card now digests differently from when it was prepared (facts._prepared, set by ws.prepared in every family's prepare), 409 'The card changed since this was prepared', before the engine is asked. What a credit's card makes is its customer, amount and currency (store_credit._makes); a code's is every value and choice on it (discounts._makes). Round 13's direct tests change the card without any withdrawal — the credit's amount, then its customer; the code's value, then its basis — and hold the old card: 409 each time, no store_credit_credit and no discount_code_create sent. Two more things hold even past that floor: each hold card carries its own amount in its execution, fixed at Prepare (store_credit: execution.input; discounts: the code's input), so a card is never applied for more than it said; and a credit is held to its balance (precondition_keys balance and currency) — round 13's test moves the balance in Admin after Prepare and the hold is `stale`, nothing sent. A duplicate needs the card to be finished-then-unlocked, which is the S2a-03 and S2b-02 defects, not a stale card.

question: Is a completion that failed classified correctly — does only a completion that provably never left give the order card back to be prepared again, so that one that left can never make a second order?
answer: The reviewer was right that the round-12 test proved nothing about the completion: test_3_a_completion_that_never_left_gives_the_card_back sets reads_fail before the hold, so the engine's precondition read of the draft fails first and draft_order_complete is never attempted (engine.commit: an exception before `sent = True` is FAILED 'service_unavailable'). Round 13's test lets every read through and fails draft_order_complete itself, before it leaves (ShopifyUnreached, `unsent`): the attempt is made once, ws.sending notes the card FAILED with Shopify's reason, the card comes back to be prepared again, and the next hold makes one order. A completion Shopify refused is given back too (ShopifyRefused, `refused`: it answered, nothing was made); one that left and cannot be read back stays locked (UNVERIFIED -> UNCONFIRMED). But a completion that LEFT and whose answer was lost is also given back when the re-read made at once shows the draft still open: ActionEngine._settle_by_observation finishes it FAILED (write.settle is None for an order) and after_commit makes the card FAILED — 'The order was not created: … Nothing was made; prepare it again.' A read timeout left the Mac (ShopifyClient._post: a plain ShopifyError, neither unsent nor refused) and Shopify can still complete it. That breaks the rule the finding asks for, and it is a real defect. What limits it: Prepare re-reads every draft the card made (shopify_order_create, facts.drafts_made) and finds an order that landed since, and an unchanged card reuses its draft, whose second completion Shopify refuses — round 13's test_t3_02_a_completion_that_left_and_landed... passes. What does not: change the card after it is given back (postage, say), and Prepare prices a NEW draft while the first is still open; Shopify then completes the first, and the hold on the new one makes a second order. Reproduced, and left failing as found (xfail strict): tests/test_r13_evidence_made_once.py::test_t3_02_a_completion_that_left_is_never_given_back_as_not_made — two completed drafts, two orders. The root is the same as S2b/S2b-02's: one re-read after an ambiguous send is taken as proof that nothing was made. The engine's commit and _settle_by_observation are identical at 6a29e310.

question: Does the objective test detect a Shopify write at all — is there a mutation ledger it checks — so that opening and changing an objective is proven to leave the shop untouched?
answer: It does now. The reviewer was right: `getattr(desk.store, 'mutations_sent', None)` compared with itself proved nothing. So round 13 changes the test (its intent kept: 'no read of the shop, no change sent') to watch the shop's `mutate` on the instance the families use (shopify_tools is bound to desk.store by the harness), counting every change asked of it whatever it is, and to cover what its docstring says: open a project, move its stage by voice, open delegated tasks, and tick one through the owner's route. It asserts: no read of the shop for any of the three spoken turns and none for the tick; the ledger empty; mutations_sent == 0, calculations == [] and drafts == []; nothing to confirm on any card. Nothing under app/objectives/ names Shopify at all: the objective tools import the objectives store, its cards, the gate's tiers and the tool registry, and nothing else of the app.

question: Does every place that sends the server's local command key check the connected far end (far_end_held_by) before sending, never follow a redirect and never go through a proxy — with launch_common's implementation in hand?
answer: Yes; the body the round-12 packet lacked is here whole (scripts/launch_common.py). The key is read in one place, launch_common._server_key (local_cli.headers(), only for a loopback URL, and only where the far end can be shown), and leaves in one: _one_connection opens the socket itself, asks _taken_by_the_service about that very socket — identity.far_end_held_by(getsockname, getpeername, the service's unit), which finds the far end's socket in /proc/net/tcp, the unit's cgroup (root-only), and a pinned pid of the unit holding that inode — and only on a yes sends the request down the same connection with http.client, which reads no proxy from the environment and follows no redirect (a 3xx is an answer). On a no nothing is sent and the key stays. call_service (the test-session commands, scripts/session_ops.call) and fetch_health (health, status, install, Control) both go through it, and _keyed_route sends the key only on its own routes (local_cli.ROUTES). The other urllib users send no key: scripts/accept.py get/post and scripts/record.py _health build requests with no local_cli header. test_the_key_leaves_through_one_function_only holds that nothing else in app/, scripts/ or experience/ reads the key to send it; the competitor tests use the real kernel check against a listener in no crooks-assistant.service cgroup.

question: Page side: once a screen named before round 10 hands its legacy key back on /displays/register, does registration rotate that key so the old one opens nothing — the server's half the page relies on?
tests: crooks-assistant/tests/web/display.test.js::a screen named before round 10 hands its key back once, stays approved, and forgets it
answer: Yes. The page (web/display.js) takes the legacy key off the device the moment it reads it (loadScreen rewrites the record to {id, name}) and hands it back once from memory, as X-Screen-Key on POST /displays/register (migrate). The server reads that header on /register alone (routes/displays.py _old_screen_key) and passes it as old_key to DisplayStore.register, which treats it exactly as holding the screen's key; for an approved screen it then runs `rotate`: screen['secret'] becomes the hash of a fresh key (secrets.token_urlsafe(24)), handed back only as the HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie (_handed), never in the answer. Every later check is DisplayStore._holds, which compares a presented key with the one stored hash, and every screen route other than /register reads only the cookie (_screen_key). So from the rotation on, the old key matches nothing: the test sends the spent key as a copier would — as the cookie — to the ask, /seen, /done, /video and /register, and each is refused, while the new cookie opens them. (Whether a rotation survives a power cut between the rename and the folder flush is the screens-server finding of the same id, class B, not this one.)

answer: The key: one per hold, from POST /voice/live (app/routes/voice.py live), which the door and the route itself both hold to the owner rule; it mints a single-use token at ElevenLabs with the server's key, refuses anything that is not key-shaped or that is the server's own key, and answers {token, url, params, expires_in_s} with no-store. live-voice.js keeps it for the life the Mac gave, counted from the ask and capped at a minute, puts it only in the URL of the one socket it opens to the wss base the Mac named, and never opens a second socket with it. The preflight's live check (round 12 record, 1.11: live_key_check.py --expiry, exit 0) found ElevenLabs' key single-use and dead after 16 minutes unused. The words: onWords is showLiveWords, which writes three text nodes marked data-spoken (#ask-words, #ask-heard, and the tablet's line under the orb while he holds); a copy of the screen masks data-spoken nodes. sendAudio posts audio, session_id, turns, speak and branch_id, and nothing else — never the words. Telemetry: the page's record callback passes only the live_transcript event, through LiveVoice.telemetryFields (fixed words and whole numbers), to web/telemetry.js, which sends to its own origin. Going out of sight cancels the live words (the visibilitychange in the live-words block) and the page's other hidden and pagehide handlers stop speaking, release the microphone, clear pointers and flush telemetry, none of which carries the words. live_transcript defaults to True (config/settings.py) and production leaves CROOKS_LIVE_TRANSCRIPT unset, so this is the configuration production would run. The page tests run app.js's own text with the real live-voice.js and telemetry.js and find neither the words nor the key in telemetry, storage, the console, any request or the address bar.

question: Did removing the fast lane (4411adde) leave a reachable write — refund, cancellation, store credit — with weaker refusal or disambiguation than before, along turn -> provider -> dispatch -> gate -> engine?
answer: No. The fast lane never wrote, so no write-side check went with it. Its own source at the commit before the deletion says so in code, and round 13's test_r13_evidence_history.py reads it from git on every run: `git show 4411adde^:crooks-assistant/app/fastpath/recipes.py` defines assert_read_only (line 111), which raised for any recipe naming a tool with a write or batch definition ('the fast lane cannot write'); app/runtime.py at that commit called it when the runtime was built (recipe_registry.assert_read_only()) and app/fastpath/runner.py before every run; and `git show 4411adde^:crooks-assistant/app/fastpath/intent.py` lists 'cancel', 'refund' and 'archive' among MUTATION_STRONG, words that took a sentence out of the lane for the model before any recipe was scored; and no recipe named any store-credit tool (a recipe naming the write shopify_store_credit_add would have stopped start-up). So a refund, a cancellation or a store credit was never the lane's to serve, before 4411adde or after. The path they take now, and took then: /turn (every new sentence withdraws what was waiting, then the model) -> MaxAgentSDKProvider (tools=[], its PreToolUse hook: owner authority, then the gate against the conversation's issued ids) -> _dispatch -> dispatch -> gate.classify -> the tool's own prepare from a fresh read -> ActionEngine.stage: a PENDING, RED card held to a gesture graver than a tap. The tests drive a refund, a cancellation and a store credit from a sentence through the scripted model and through the real provider: each is a red card on the record read, a commit without the hold is 409 not_armed, a spoken yes applies nothing, a record the conversation never read is denied by the hook, and the shop receives nothing.

question: What does a screen's own 'Mark packed' mean: may an approved screen's tap, which the server cannot tell from a key holder's paced requests, be recorded as packed at all?
answer: Left for George's ruling. The reviewer is right about the mechanism: an approved screen's key holder that paces its /seen requests to the server's own plan and then posts /done with confirm true gets a done row, and the server cannot tell that from a packer's tap — round 10's test does exactly that. question: Does every module import at this SHA, does every import resolve, does nothing name a module deleted with the fast lane, and does test-session capture run — settled by executing it rather than by reading two modules?
answer: Yes, by execution at this exact SHA. Acceptance run 36567654914 (workflow 'acceptance', event push, clive/trunk, head_sha 361b01380737f8f48020dd30cef1e5f750e700bb, job 109403584488, conclusion success) recorded in its provenance: candidate_sha 361b0138…, clean worktree, and the gate pytest_offline_full — `python -m pytest tests -m "not live" -q -p no:cacheprovider` — exit 0, '5946 passed, 26 skipped, 2 deselected in 350.26s'; ruff 'All checks passed!'; secret scan 'no leaks found'. The log is quiet (-q), so it has no line per test; neither tests/test_no_dangling_imports.py nor tests/test_r11_records.py carries a skip mark or a live mark, so every test named here was among the 5946 that passed. They pass again at this commit locally (20 passed). What they do: every module under app/ is imported by name; every import statement in app/, experience/, scripts/, tests/ and bench/ — at the top of a file or inside a function — names a module that exists and a name it has; no dotted string names a deleted module and each deleted one is really gone; in a fresh interpreter every module under app/, scripts/ and config/ imports and every lazy import in them resolves; and app.families.load_all() returns every family module the package holds (load_all only logs a failed family, so this comparison is what would show one). Start-up under production's configuration is the deploy's own restart and /health.
